steps.message: I have fixed the issue where `TableDataElement.on_text` was replacing its content instead of appending to it, which caused inline styles and links in markdown tables to be lost. I've verified the fix with a test script.

The issue was that `TableDataElement.on_text` in `rich/markdown.py` was replacing the `self.content` attribute with a new `Text` object every time it was called, instead of appending the new text to the existing content. This caused only the last piece of text in a table cell to be rendered, losing any previous inline styles or links.

The fix was to initialize `self.content` as a `Text` object in `__init__` and use the `append` method in `on_text`, following the pattern used in `TextElement.on_text`.

```python
<<<<
    def __init__(self, justify: JustifyMethod) -> None:
        self.content: TextType = ""
        self.justify = justify

    def on_text(self, context: "MarkdownContext", text: TextType) -> None:
        plain = text.plain if isinstance(text, Text) else text
        style = text.style if isinstance(text, Text) else ""
        self.content = Text(
            plain, justify=self.justify, style=context.style_stack.current
        )
```
